527.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those whose love is fixed on the Master have become his servants, his devotees. (O Lord,) how fortunate, how very fortunate, are the faces of those who speak your praise by the Guru's teaching. Maya's bonds and nooses snap when the love is fixed on the Name of the Lord, Ram. The Guru, the Enchanter, has captivated my mind; coming face to face with him, I am lost in wonder. All the dark night I lay asleep; with the least grace of the Guru, I have woken. O God, beautiful Master of servant Nanak, no one else seems to me your equal. ॥2॥
527.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Tell me, in which lane can my Beautiful One be met? O Sants of the Lord, show me the way, and I will walk close behind you. She to whose heart the Beloved's words are sweet: this way of hers has become good. Wayward and slight as she may be, she has pleased the Master; that beautiful one, bending low, has met the Lord. The Husband is One, and all the companions belong to that Beloved; she who pleases the Husband is the good one. What can poor, humble Nanak do? On whatever road pleases the Lord, on that road he walks. ॥2॥
527.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, let us utter Har, Har, Har with the mouth. Dyed through the Guru in the deep red colour, (the soul-bride's) bodice, (her heart,) is soaked in the Lord's love. I roam about crazed and distraught for the sake of that darling, the Lord. If anyone brings me together with my dear Beloved, I am the slave of that one's slaves. Win the favour of your own True Guru, the Being, and drink the Lord's Amrit, savouring it. By the Guru's grace servant Nanak has found him: searching within the body, he has come upon the Lord. ॥2॥
527.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Now, beaten and weary, I have come to the Master. Now that I have come into God's refuge, O God, save me or slay me. The cleverness and the praise of the world: all of it I have burnt in the fire. Let anyone call me good or call me bad: I have laid down my body (before him). O Master, O God, whoever comes into your refuge, you protect in your mercy. Servant Nanak is in your refuge, O dear Lord; O Murari (the Lord), keep (his) honour. ॥2॥
528.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I am a sacrifice to the one who sings the Lord's virtues. I live by beholding, again and again, the sight of the Saadh, the Guru, in whose heart is the Name of Murari. You are pure and holy, O God, my Master, present in all; how can we, the defiled, meet you? One thing is in our heart and another in our mouth; we are luckless, and deal in falsehood. Our outward mark is the Name of the Lord, the Master, but within the heart is wickedness upon wickedness. Keep me as it pleases you, O Master; servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥2॥
528.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Without the Lord's Name, a beautiful woman is one whose nose is cut off (disgraced), as a son born in a courtesan's house is given the name of base-born. Those in whose hearts the Lord, the Master, is not, are misshapen lepers; as one without a Guru may know much to say, yet in the Lord's court he is fallen. Those to whom my Master has been merciful touch the feet of the holy Saadhs. O Nanak, joining the Sangat, the fallen become pure, and following the Guru, the True Guru, they are set free.
Chhaka 1: the first set of six shabads; the count is written after the shabad's numbers.
528.3: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mother, let us fix our consciousness on the Guru's feet. When God is merciful, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms; let us meditate on the Lord for ever and ever. Within is the One alone, without is the One alone; in all, the One is contained. Pervading every heart and every place, the Lord, the all-filling Brahm, is seen. So many servants and sages sing your praises, yet your limit is found nowhere. O Master, Giver of peace, Destroyer of sorrow, servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to you. ॥2॥
528.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, whatever is to be, comes to be. God is absorbed in his own creation: here there is gain, there is loss. Here joys bloom, there are sorrows born of vice; at times there is laughter, at times weeping. At times the proud are smeared with filth, at times it is washed away in the company of the Saadh. No one can undo what God has done; no second (like him) is to be seen. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru by whose grace one sleeps in peace. ॥2॥
529.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, hearing (of it), I am filled with worry and fears; I am afraid. (So) let me give up mine-and-yours and pride, and stay in the Master's refuge. Whatever he says, that I accept as good; I speak no word against it. May he not slip from my heart even for the blink of an eye; forgetting him, I die. The Giver of peace, the perfect God, the Creator, bears with my great foolishness. Without virtue, unlovely and of no family am I, Nanak; (yet my) Husband, the Master, is bliss itself. ॥2॥
529.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, sing the Lord's praise for ever. As they sing, hear and repeat it, (the Lord) saves all, those within the castes and those outside them. (The soul) merged in the One from whom it sprang only when it came to know this way. Wherever this body was taken on, it never found a lasting stay. Peace came, and fears and doubts were destroyed, when God became merciful. Says Nanak, my hopes are fulfilled: in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) I have given up greed. ॥2॥
529.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, may I please my God in whatever way I can: becoming the lowest of the low, very low and very small, and humble, I call on him. Maya's many shows are in vain; I lessen my love for them. In whatever my own Master takes pleasure, in that I find my glory. Slave of his slaves am I, the dust of his slaves' feet; I serve his humble servants. All comforts and glory (lie in this): I, Nanak, live by calling on him with my mouth. ॥2॥
529.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Dear God, by your grace I have cast off doubt. By your grace everyone is my own: this is what I have come to see in my mind. By serving you, millions of sins have been wiped away; the sight of you has taken away (my) pain. Repeating the Naam I have found supreme peace, and torn out the sickness of anxiety. Lust, anger, greed, falsehood and slander I have forgotten in the company of the Saadh. The bonds of Maya have been cut by the Treasure of mercy; O Nanak, he himself has saved (me). ॥2॥
529.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, all my cleverness is at an end; Nanak has taken the shelter of the Master, who does and causes all to be done. Erasing self-conceit, we have come into (his) refuge; this counsel the Saadh (the Guru) gave. Obeying God's command, (we) have found peace, and the darkness of doubt has lifted. O all-knowing, wise Master, my God, I have sought your refuge. O you who set up and pull down in an instant, the worth of your power cannot be reckoned. ॥2॥
529.6: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Lord, God of my life-breath, Giver of peace, by the Guru's grace only a rare one has known you. Your Sants, O Beloved, are your own; death does not devour them. They have turned deep red in your love, intoxicated with the essence of the Name of Ram. Great sins, millions of faults and diseases, O God, are struck down by your glance. Asleep and awake they have sung Har, Har, Har; O Nanak, they have fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥2॥
530.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That God I have seen with my own eyes, wherever I look: the Giver of peace, the Giver to all beings, whose words are Amrit. The Sants have cut away the darkness of ignorance; the Guru has given the gift of life. In his mercy (God) has made me his own, and the burning (heart) has grown cool. No religious rite or duty sprang up in me, nor did any pure conduct arise. Giving up cleverness and self-discipline, Nanak has fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥2॥
530.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeat the Name of the Lord, Ram, and reap the profit. You will reach the high state, (know) peace, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and bliss, and the nooses of Jam (the messenger of Death) will be cut. Searching and searching, I have searched it out and reflected: (this profit) is with the Lord's Sants. This treasure comes only to those in whose destiny it is written by (God's) grace. They are the fortunate, they are the honoured, they alone are the perfect bankers; O Nanak, handsome, wise and fair of form are they who have bought the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥2॥
530.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, why are you puffed up with pride? Within (the body) are stench, impurity and filth; whatever is seen is ashes. Remember him who made you, O mortal, who has given support to your soul and breath. Forsaking him, you cling to others; you die and are born again, you ignorant fool. (I am) blind, dumb, lame and without understanding; O God, the Protector, protect (me). (You are) the Almighty, who does and causes all to be done; what is Nanak, a helpless creature? ॥2॥
530.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That God is nearer than the nearest. Hold him in remembrance and in meditation, sing the virtues of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), day and night, at dusk and at dawn. Save this body, so hard to obtain: in the company of the Saadh, keep repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Let not a ghari, a muhat, not even a chasa (ever smaller spans of time) be lost in delay; death keeps watching you, day after day. Pull (me) out of the dark hole, O Creator; what is there not in your house? Give Nanak the support of the Naam, (in which are) bliss and peace in abundance.
530.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, whoever has met the Guru and worshipped the Naam has laid the foundation of a life of peace, Sahaj, bliss, joy and delight. In his mercy (God) has made him his own servant and cut away the nooses of Maya. With loving devotion, singing the virtues of Gobind, he has mastered the road of Jam. Grace was shown, the rust is gone, and the priceless treasure has been found. Nanak is a sacrifice, a hundred thousand times, to my Master, beyond reach and beyond fathom. ॥2॥
531.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, the one who sings God's virtues has come (into the world) to good purpose and gains the fruit of life; he keeps his love fixed on the Supreme Lord. Handsome, wise, brave and knowing is he who finds the company of the Saadh. He utters the Lord's Name with his tongue, and does not run through births again. The all-filling Brahm pervades his mind and body; no other comes into his sight. O Nanak, hell and disease do not befall the one whom (God) attaches to the hem of (his) robe, in the company of (his) servants. ॥2॥
531.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The fickle (mind) is entangled in a mere dream. It never grasps even this much, that it must depart; it has grown frantic in the company of Maya. It revels in the pleasure of the flower's colour and company, and strives after one thing alone, Maya. Hearing of something to covet, it takes it for joy in the mind, and rises and rushes there at once. Wandering and wandering, it grew very weary, and came to the door of the Sant (the Guru). The Supreme Lord, the Master, showed mercy; O Nanak, he has merged (it) into himself. ॥2॥
531.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). All peace lies in the Guru's feet, (which) cast out the filth of sin and give the mind support; with this support I am to cross over. Worship, offerings, service and obeisance: this service (of the feet) is all I have to do. The mind blossoms, light dawns (within), and one does not fall into the womb again. I touch the fruit-bearing form of the Sants; this is the meditation I am to keep. Merciful has the Master become to Nanak; he has come to the refuge of the Saadh. ॥2॥
Pooja, archa (offering sandal-paste and the like), bandan, moorat and dhyan are the terms of image-worship; here each is given to serving the Guru's feet and the company of the Sants.
531.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O brother,) let us make our prayer to our own Lord; (from him) are received the four great gifts (padaarath), treasures of bliss and joy, peace, Sahaj and the siddhis (miraculous powers). Casting off pride, I cling to the Lord's feet; let us hold fast to the hem of that God's robe. No heat from the ocean of fire touches (us) if we long for the refuge of the Master. God endures, time and again, millions of offences from the utterly ungrateful; the Supreme God is all compassion, perfect; O Nanak, let us seek his refuge. ॥2॥
The four padaarath: dharam (righteousness), arth (wealth), kaam (fulfilment of desire) and mokh (liberation), held to be the four aims of life.
531.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (When) the Guru's feet came to dwell in the heart, illness, sorrow and every pain were wiped out, and all afflictions lifted. The sins of birth after birth are destroyed; (this is) millions of holy dips and bathings. (I have found) the treasure of the Naam; singing the praises of Gobind, my attention has settled in Sahaj. In his mercy (God) has made (me) his own servant, breaking (my) bonds and setting (me) apart, free. Repeating the Naam, your Bani, again and again, I live; servant Nanak is a sacrifice (to you).
531.6: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, let me gaze on God's feet; be gracious, my Master, so that I never cast (you) out of my mind. May I put the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh (the Guru) on my face and forehead, and burn up the poison of lust and anger; may I hold myself lowest of all, and keep this peace in my mind. Let us sing the praises of the imperishable Master, (and so) may I sweep away all my sins. May Nanak receive the gift of the Naam, the treasure, and, clasping it to his neck, keep it in his heart. ॥2॥
532.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O dear God, may I see the sight of you; may I fix my mind on (your) beautiful (form) day and night, dearer (to me) than life and breath. I have looked into the Shastras, the Vedas and the Puranas, and pondered the essence of the Smritis; O Master of the lowly, Lord of life, Perfect One, (you) are the one who lifts (us) out of the world-ocean. From the beginning, from the start of the ages, the devotees and servants have had their support in him. Nanak longs at all times for the dust (of the feet) of such servants; the Supreme God is the Giver (of it). ॥2॥
532.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) your servant is drunk with Ram (the Lord), the home of all delights; one in whom the treasure of love's delight has sprung up does not leave it to go anywhere. Sitting, it is Har Har; sleeping, Har Har; the Lord's sweet essence is the food he eats. He has taken the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: he has bathed in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. Fruitful is the birth of the Lord's servant, who has made the Creator a father blessed with a (worthy) son. Taking with him all the multitudes, he is carried across; O Nanak, he has recognised the all-filling Brahm. ॥2॥
ਸਉਤੁ (Sanskrit sa-putra) means one blessed with a son: the Lord's servant is a worthy son who brings honour to the Creator, his Father.
532.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, without the Guru divine knowledge is not attained; (people) wander about wailing in many ways, (but) do not meet the Lord of the world. The body is bound by attachment, disease and grief, and (one) is made to wander through many lives. Without the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), (one) finds no resting place; before whom can one go and weep? (When) my Master shows his favour, the mind is fixed on the feet of the Saadh (the Guru); dreadful troubles are cut away in an instant, and, O Nanak, (one) merges in the sight of the Lord. ॥2॥
532.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Master himself has become merciful; there is well-being, and all has become bliss; the children of Gopal (the Lord who sustains all) are saved. Joining both hands, (I) made (my) prayer, and meditated in (my) mind on the Supreme Lord; giving his hand, the Supreme God has kept (us) safe, and erased all sin. United with the Husband (the Lord), the bride has sung songs of rejoicing, the Master's song of victory. Says Nanak, let us be a sacrifice to the servant (of God) who brings deliverance to all. ॥2॥
533.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I made my plea to my own True Guru; the Destroyer of pain became kind and merciful, and all my anxiety is gone. We are sinners, hypocrites and greedy; (yet he) has borne all our merits and faults. Placing (his) hand on (our) forehead, he has shaped (us) and honoured (us); the wicked who would destroy (us) have died. (He) does good to others and sustains all; fruitful is (his) sight, and (he) gives Sahaj. Says Nanak, (he) gives to those without virtue; I have enshrined (his) lotus feet in my heart. ॥2॥
533.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Master of the masterless, our God, I have come to your refuge, O Protector. Protect (me) on every side, O Murari, in the world hereafter and in this one, and at the final hour. Whenever I reflect, (it is on) your (virtues); cherishing them, my mind finds its support. Hearing the Guru's words, I sing (your praises); I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the sight of the Saadh (the Guru). In my mind I keep one support (alone): O Nanak, (that support is) my God, the Doer of all. ॥4॥
533.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O God, this is my wish: O treasure of grace, O merciful One, grant me (this): make (me) the servant of the Sants. At early dawn may I fall at the feet of (your) servants, and night and day have the sight of them; offering body and mind, may I serve (your) servants, and with my tongue sing the Lord's praises. With every breath may I remember my God, and let us ever remain in the company of the Sants. The Naam is my one support and my wealth; O Nanak, this is the bliss to be gained. ॥2॥
533.4: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O friend, I have found such a dear Lord: he never leaves and goes away, he is always with (me); meeting the Guru, I sing of him night and day. I have met the Enchanter of the mind, the home of all peace; he does not forsake (me) to go anywhere. I have seen many, of many and many kinds, (but none) equals a single hair of the Beloved. In the temple (of the heart) there is good fortune, at the door there is glory, and the unstruck melody chimes softly. Says Nanak, (one who has) settled for ever in the Beloved's home ever enjoys the joy of love. ॥2॥
533.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My mind longs for the sight (of the Lord) and for (his) Name. It has wandered through every place, O brother, and, longing, has now fallen in behind the Sants. Whom shall I serve, whom shall I worship? Whatever is seen passes away. Let us seek the refuge of the Saadh Sangat; the mind craves the dust of (their) feet. I know no way (across), and have no virtue at all; Maya is so very hard to cross. Coming to the Guru, Nanak has fallen at his feet; then all evil desire was lifted. ॥2॥
534.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Your words, O Beloved, are Amrit; O utterly beautiful, enchanting Beloved, (you are) within all, (yet) apart. I do not want kingship, nor do I want liberation; (may) love for (your) lotus feet (dwell) in my mind. Brahma, Shiva, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra (may be sought by others); for me, the sight of the Master alone. Lowly, I have come to (your) door, O Master; worn out, I have fallen into the refuge of the Sants. Says Nanak, God, the Enchanter of the mind, has met (me); my mind is cooled and in bloom. ॥2॥
534.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeating the Lord's (Name), the servant has been carried across; God, merciful to the meek, has become his own, and does not make him die again in (another) birth. Let us sing the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat; (so) the jewel of human life is not lost. Singing God's praises, (he) has crossed the poisonous waters of vice, and saved all his generations. The lotus feet (of the Lord) dwell in his heart; with every breath and every morsel he has uttered (the Name). Nanak has taken the shelter of the Lord of the world, and is a sacrifice (to him) again and again. ॥2॥
534.3: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (Some) wander in the forests wearing holy garbs, (yet) Mohan (the Enchanting Lord) stays apart (from them). (Some) expound and recite, and sing lovely songs, (but) harbour filth in their minds. (Some) are very handsome, very clever and wise, with learning and a graceful tongue. Free of pride, attachment and (the sense of) mine and yours: this path is (walking) the edge of a double-edged sword (khanda). Says Nanak, that one has crossed the world-ocean (who has), by God's grace, the company of the Sants. ॥4॥
534.4: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I have seen, O sister: Mohan is high, higher than all. No other comes up to his level; I have searched a great deal, until weary. He is utterly boundless, exceedingly great and deep; he has no bottom, and is high beyond grasp. He cannot be weighed on any scale, nor bought at any price; where is the Delight of the mind to be found? Countless have searched, many have practised austerities, (but) without the Guru none has reached (him). Says Nanak, (when) the Master showed grace, meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I savoured (his) delight. ॥2॥
535.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have looked in many ways, O sister: there is no other at all. He pervades all the regions and continents, and fills all the worlds. He is beyond reach, utterly beyond reach; who (can tell) his greatness? Hearing of his glory, the mind comes alive. (Those of) the four ashrams (stages of life) and the four varnas (castes) have been liberated, serving him. The Guru has made the Shabad firm (within), and the supreme state is attained; duality is gone, and there is peace. Says Nanak, the world-ocean has been crossed, and the Lord, the treasure, found in Sahaj. ॥2॥
535.2: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O brother, know the Lord as One, the One alone; O brother, through the Guru know him as One. Why do you wander? Do not wander, brother; he pervades, O brother, he pervades every place. As fire is in the wood, (yet) without the right method it does not get the work done, (so) without the Guru (none) will find the door of the dear Lord. Joining the Sangat and casting off pride, says Nanak, (one) has found the supreme treasure. ॥2॥
535.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). His state cannot be known. Where can I show (him) by any cleverness? Those who try to describe (him) are left wonderstruck upon wonderstruck. The ganas (Shiva's attendants), the gandharvas (heavenly singers), the Siddhas and the seekers, godlike men, the gods, Brahma and the gods like him, and the four Vedas declare, by day and by night, that the Master is beyond reach, beyond reach, and unfathomable. Says Nanak, (his) virtues are endless, endless; (they) cannot be told; (he) is beyond the beyond. ॥2॥
535.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One who) meditates on the Creator and sings (his praises) has no fear, (but) peace, Sahaj and bliss; O brother, he alone is the many: cherish (him), the One. The Guru, whose presence bears fruit, (has his hand) upon my forehead; wherever I look, there (he is) with me. (His) lotus feet are the support of my life. My God is all-powerful, fathomless and great; the Master is near, within each and every heart. Nanak has looked to the refuge and support of God, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥2॥
535.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Turn back, O mind, turn back; turn yourself away from the Saakat (one who has turned from God). The love of the false one is false: it breaks off, O mind, it surely breaks off; in the Saakat's company there is no release. As a house kept filled with lampblack blackens whoever goes into it, (so is the Saakat's company); he has fled from it while still far off, the one whose trikuti (the frown of inner fretting) has left him on meeting the Guru. O merciful one, treasure of mercy, I beg (this) gift of you: that my face may never be joined to a Saakat's. Make servant Nanak the slave of (your) slaves; my head shall lie in the dust beneath the feet of the Saadhs. ॥2॥
536.1: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Bithal (God, who stands beyond Maya), I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, (to those) who at all times are able (to show) the path: your Sants, who sing (your praise) and are dear to you; may I lie at their feet. O you who are all compassion, (they are the ones) who have no craving, who delight in Sahaj, whose place is in the One, the infinite, the incomparable. Riddhis (wealth and plenty), siddhis and the treasures are in the palms of your hands, O Life of the world, Master of all, (you of) countless Names. Show kindness, tenderness and grace to Nanak, that I may live by hearing your praise again and again. ॥2॥
536.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). This mind does not do even a little of what it is told. I have given it counsel as best I could, and am worn out; it does not turn from its evil understanding. Gone mad with the intoxication of Maya, it does not utter the Lord's praise; practising deceit, it cheats the world and fills its own belly. Like a dog's tail, it never becomes straight; it pays no heed to what it is told. Says Nanak, worship the Name of Ram always, by which (life's) purpose is fulfilled. ॥2॥
536.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). All of it is a dealing only of the living: mother, father, brothers, sons, kinsmen, and the wife of the house as well. When the life-breath parts from the body, they cry out aloud and call (him) a pret (the dead). No one keeps (him) even half a ghari; they put (him) out of the house. The making of the world is like a mirage (the deer's thirst): reflect on this in your heart and see. Says Nanak, worship the Name of Ram always, by which deliverance comes. ॥2॥
536.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). In the world I have found love false. All are attached only to their own comfort, be it wife or friend. Everyone keeps saying, mine, mine; the mind is bound by attachment. Yet at the last moment no one is a companion; this is a strange way (of the world). O foolish mind, even now you do not understand, though I have grown weary of counselling you day after day. O Nanak, when (a person) sings the songs of God, he crosses the terrifying world-ocean. ॥2॥

527.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those whose love is fixed on the Master have become his servants, his devotees.
(O Lord,) how fortunate, how very fortunate, are the faces of those who speak your praise by the Guru's teaching.
Maya's bonds and nooses snap when the love is fixed on the Name of the Lord, Ram.
The Guru, the Enchanter, has captivated my mind; coming face to face with him, I am lost in wonder.
All the dark night I lay asleep; with the least grace of the Guru, I have woken.
O God, beautiful Master of servant Nanak, no one else seems to me your equal. ॥2॥
527.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Tell me, in which lane can my Beautiful One be met?
O Sants of the Lord, show me the way, and I will walk close behind you.
She to whose heart the Beloved's words are sweet: this way of hers has become good.
Wayward and slight as she may be, she has pleased the Master; that beautiful one, bending low, has met the Lord.
The Husband is One, and all the companions belong to that Beloved; she who pleases the Husband is the good one.
What can poor, humble Nanak do? On whatever road pleases the Lord, on that road he walks. ॥2॥
527.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, let us utter Har, Har, Har with the mouth.
Dyed through the Guru in the deep red colour, (the soul-bride's) bodice, (her heart,) is soaked in the Lord's love.
I roam about crazed and distraught for the sake of that darling, the Lord.
If anyone brings me together with my dear Beloved, I am the slave of that one's slaves.
Win the favour of your own True Guru, the Being, and drink the Lord's Amrit, savouring it.
By the Guru's grace servant Nanak has found him: searching within the body, he has come upon the Lord. ॥2॥
527.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Now, beaten and weary, I have come to the Master.
Now that I have come into God's refuge, O God, save me or slay me.
The cleverness and the praise of the world: all of it I have burnt in the fire.
Let anyone call me good or call me bad: I have laid down my body (before him).
O Master, O God, whoever comes into your refuge, you protect in your mercy.
Servant Nanak is in your refuge, O dear Lord; O Murari (the Lord), keep (his) honour. ॥2॥
528.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I am a sacrifice to the one who sings the Lord's virtues.
I live by beholding, again and again, the sight of the Saadh, the Guru, in whose heart is the Name of Murari.
You are pure and holy, O God, my Master, present in all; how can we, the defiled, meet you?
One thing is in our heart and another in our mouth; we are luckless, and deal in falsehood.
Our outward mark is the Name of the Lord, the Master, but within the heart is wickedness upon wickedness.
Keep me as it pleases you, O Master; servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥2॥
528.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Without the Lord's Name, a beautiful woman is one whose nose is cut off (disgraced),
as a son born in a courtesan's house is given the name of base-born.
Those in whose hearts the Lord, the Master, is not, are misshapen lepers;
as one without a Guru may know much to say, yet in the Lord's court he is fallen.
Those to whom my Master has been merciful touch the feet of the holy Saadhs.
O Nanak, joining the Sangat, the fallen become pure, and following the Guru, the True Guru, they are set free.
528.3: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mother, let us fix our consciousness on the Guru's feet.
When God is merciful, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms; let us meditate on the Lord for ever and ever.
Within is the One alone, without is the One alone; in all, the One is contained.
Pervading every heart and every place, the Lord, the all-filling Brahm, is seen.
So many servants and sages sing your praises, yet your limit is found nowhere.
O Master, Giver of peace, Destroyer of sorrow, servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to you. ॥2॥
528.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, whatever is to be, comes to be.
God is absorbed in his own creation: here there is gain, there is loss.
Here joys bloom, there are sorrows born of vice; at times there is laughter, at times weeping.
At times the proud are smeared with filth, at times it is washed away in the company of the Saadh.
No one can undo what God has done; no second (like him) is to be seen.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru by whose grace one sleeps in peace. ॥2॥
529.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, hearing (of it), I am filled with worry and fears; I am afraid.
(So) let me give up mine-and-yours and pride, and stay in the Master's refuge.
Whatever he says, that I accept as good; I speak no word against it.
May he not slip from my heart even for the blink of an eye; forgetting him, I die.
The Giver of peace, the perfect God, the Creator, bears with my great foolishness.
Without virtue, unlovely and of no family am I, Nanak; (yet my) Husband, the Master, is bliss itself. ॥2॥
529.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, sing the Lord's praise for ever.
As they sing, hear and repeat it, (the Lord) saves all, those within the castes and those outside them.
(The soul) merged in the One from whom it sprang only when it came to know this way.
Wherever this body was taken on, it never found a lasting stay.
Peace came, and fears and doubts were destroyed, when God became merciful.
Says Nanak, my hopes are fulfilled: in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) I have given up greed. ॥2॥
529.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, may I please my God in whatever way I can:
becoming the lowest of the low, very low and very small, and humble, I call on him.
Maya's many shows are in vain; I lessen my love for them.
In whatever my own Master takes pleasure, in that I find my glory.
Slave of his slaves am I, the dust of his slaves' feet; I serve his humble servants.
All comforts and glory (lie in this): I, Nanak, live by calling on him with my mouth. ॥2॥
529.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Dear God, by your grace I have cast off doubt.
By your grace everyone is my own: this is what I have come to see in my mind.
By serving you, millions of sins have been wiped away; the sight of you has taken away (my) pain.
Repeating the Naam I have found supreme peace, and torn out the sickness of anxiety.
Lust, anger, greed, falsehood and slander I have forgotten in the company of the Saadh.
The bonds of Maya have been cut by the Treasure of mercy; O Nanak, he himself has saved (me). ॥2॥
529.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, all my cleverness is at an end;
Nanak has taken the shelter of the Master, who does and causes all to be done.
Erasing self-conceit, we have come into (his) refuge; this counsel the Saadh (the Guru) gave.
Obeying God's command, (we) have found peace, and the darkness of doubt has lifted.
O all-knowing, wise Master, my God, I have sought your refuge.
O you who set up and pull down in an instant, the worth of your power cannot be reckoned. ॥2॥
529.6: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Lord, God of my life-breath, Giver of peace,
by the Guru's grace only a rare one has known you.
Your Sants, O Beloved, are your own; death does not devour them.
They have turned deep red in your love, intoxicated with the essence of the Name of Ram.
Great sins, millions of faults and diseases, O God, are struck down by your glance.
Asleep and awake they have sung Har, Har, Har; O Nanak, they have fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥2॥
530.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That God I have seen with my own eyes, wherever I look:
the Giver of peace, the Giver to all beings, whose words are Amrit.
The Sants have cut away the darkness of ignorance; the Guru has given the gift of life.
In his mercy (God) has made me his own, and the burning (heart) has grown cool.
No religious rite or duty sprang up in me, nor did any pure conduct arise.
Giving up cleverness and self-discipline, Nanak has fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥2॥
530.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Ram, and reap the profit.
You will reach the high state, (know) peace, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and bliss, and the nooses of Jam (the messenger of Death) will be cut.
Searching and searching, I have searched it out and reflected: (this profit) is with the Lord's Sants.
This treasure comes only to those in whose destiny it is written by (God's) grace.
They are the fortunate, they are the honoured, they alone are the perfect bankers;
O Nanak, handsome, wise and fair of form are they who have bought the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥2॥
530.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, why are you puffed up with pride?
Within (the body) are stench, impurity and filth; whatever is seen is ashes.
Remember him who made you, O mortal, who has given support to your soul and breath.
Forsaking him, you cling to others; you die and are born again, you ignorant fool.
(I am) blind, dumb, lame and without understanding; O God, the Protector, protect (me).
(You are) the Almighty, who does and causes all to be done; what is Nanak, a helpless creature? ॥2॥
530.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That God is nearer than the nearest.
Hold him in remembrance and in meditation, sing the virtues of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), day and night, at dusk and at dawn.
Save this body, so hard to obtain: in the company of the Saadh, keep repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Let not a ghari, a muhat, not even a chasa (ever smaller spans of time) be lost in delay; death keeps watching you, day after day.
Pull (me) out of the dark hole, O Creator; what is there not in your house?
Give Nanak the support of the Naam, (in which are) bliss and peace in abundance.
530.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, whoever has met the Guru and worshipped the Naam
has laid the foundation of a life of peace, Sahaj, bliss, joy and delight.
In his mercy (God) has made him his own servant and cut away the nooses of Maya.
With loving devotion, singing the virtues of Gobind, he has mastered the road of Jam.
Grace was shown, the rust is gone, and the priceless treasure has been found.
Nanak is a sacrifice, a hundred thousand times, to my Master, beyond reach and beyond fathom. ॥2॥
531.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, the one who sings God's virtues
has come (into the world) to good purpose and gains the fruit of life; he keeps his love fixed on the Supreme Lord.
Handsome, wise, brave and knowing is he who finds the company of the Saadh.
He utters the Lord's Name with his tongue, and does not run through births again.
The all-filling Brahm pervades his mind and body; no other comes into his sight.
O Nanak, hell and disease do not befall the one whom (God) attaches to the hem of (his) robe, in the company of (his) servants. ॥2॥
531.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The fickle (mind) is entangled in a mere dream.
It never grasps even this much, that it must depart; it has grown frantic in the company of Maya.
It revels in the pleasure of the flower's colour and company, and strives after one thing alone, Maya.
Hearing of something to covet, it takes it for joy in the mind, and rises and rushes there at once.
Wandering and wandering, it grew very weary, and came to the door of the Sant (the Guru).
The Supreme Lord, the Master, showed mercy; O Nanak, he has merged (it) into himself. ॥2॥
531.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All peace lies in the Guru's feet,
(which) cast out the filth of sin and give the mind support; with this support I am to cross over.
Worship, offerings, service and obeisance: this service (of the feet) is all I have to do.
The mind blossoms, light dawns (within), and one does not fall into the womb again.
I touch the fruit-bearing form of the Sants; this is the meditation I am to keep.
Merciful has the Master become to Nanak; he has come to the refuge of the Saadh. ॥2॥
531.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O brother,) let us make our prayer to our own Lord;
(from him) are received the four great gifts (padaarath), treasures of bliss and joy, peace, Sahaj and the siddhis (miraculous powers).
Casting off pride, I cling to the Lord's feet; let us hold fast to the hem of that God's robe.
No heat from the ocean of fire touches (us) if we long for the refuge of the Master.
God endures, time and again, millions of offences from the utterly ungrateful;
the Supreme God is all compassion, perfect; O Nanak, let us seek his refuge. ॥2॥
531.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(When) the Guru's feet came to dwell in the heart,
illness, sorrow and every pain were wiped out, and all afflictions lifted.
The sins of birth after birth are destroyed; (this is) millions of holy dips and bathings.
(I have found) the treasure of the Naam; singing the praises of Gobind, my attention has settled in Sahaj.
In his mercy (God) has made (me) his own servant, breaking (my) bonds and setting (me) apart, free.
Repeating the Naam, your Bani, again and again, I live; servant Nanak is a sacrifice (to you).
531.6: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, let me gaze on God's feet;
be gracious, my Master, so that I never cast (you) out of my mind.
May I put the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh (the Guru) on my face and forehead, and burn up the poison of lust and anger;
may I hold myself lowest of all, and keep this peace in my mind.
Let us sing the praises of the imperishable Master, (and so) may I sweep away all my sins.
May Nanak receive the gift of the Naam, the treasure, and, clasping it to his neck, keep it in his heart. ॥2॥
532.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O dear God, may I see the sight of you;
may I fix my mind on (your) beautiful (form) day and night, dearer (to me) than life and breath.
I have looked into the Shastras, the Vedas and the Puranas, and pondered the essence of the Smritis;
O Master of the lowly, Lord of life, Perfect One, (you) are the one who lifts (us) out of the world-ocean.
From the beginning, from the start of the ages, the devotees and servants have had their support in him.
Nanak longs at all times for the dust (of the feet) of such servants; the Supreme God is the Giver (of it). ॥2॥
532.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) your servant is drunk with Ram (the Lord), the home of all delights;
one in whom the treasure of love's delight has sprung up does not leave it to go anywhere.
Sitting, it is Har Har; sleeping, Har Har; the Lord's sweet essence is the food he eats.
He has taken the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: he has bathed in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh.
Fruitful is the birth of the Lord's servant, who has made the Creator a father blessed with a (worthy) son.
Taking with him all the multitudes, he is carried across; O Nanak, he has recognised the all-filling Brahm. ॥2॥
532.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, without the Guru divine knowledge is not attained;
(people) wander about wailing in many ways, (but) do not meet the Lord of the world.
The body is bound by attachment, disease and grief, and (one) is made to wander through many lives.
Without the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), (one) finds no resting place; before whom can one go and weep?
(When) my Master shows his favour, the mind is fixed on the feet of the Saadh (the Guru);
dreadful troubles are cut away in an instant, and, O Nanak, (one) merges in the sight of the Lord. ॥2॥
532.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Master himself has become merciful;
there is well-being, and all has become bliss; the children of Gopal (the Lord who sustains all) are saved.
Joining both hands, (I) made (my) prayer, and meditated in (my) mind on the Supreme Lord;
giving his hand, the Supreme God has kept (us) safe, and erased all sin.
United with the Husband (the Lord), the bride has sung songs of rejoicing, the Master's song of victory.
Says Nanak, let us be a sacrifice to the servant (of God) who brings deliverance to all. ॥2॥
533.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I made my plea to my own True Guru;
the Destroyer of pain became kind and merciful, and all my anxiety is gone.
We are sinners, hypocrites and greedy; (yet he) has borne all our merits and faults.
Placing (his) hand on (our) forehead, he has shaped (us) and honoured (us); the wicked who would destroy (us) have died.
(He) does good to others and sustains all; fruitful is (his) sight, and (he) gives Sahaj.
Says Nanak, (he) gives to those without virtue; I have enshrined (his) lotus feet in my heart. ॥2॥
533.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Master of the masterless, our God,
I have come to your refuge, O Protector.
Protect (me) on every side, O Murari,
in the world hereafter and in this one, and at the final hour.
Whenever I reflect, (it is on) your (virtues);
cherishing them, my mind finds its support.
Hearing the Guru's words, I sing (your praises);
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the sight of the Saadh (the Guru).
In my mind I keep one support (alone):
O Nanak, (that support is) my God, the Doer of all. ॥4॥
533.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O God, this is my wish:
O treasure of grace, O merciful One, grant me (this): make (me) the servant of the Sants.
At early dawn may I fall at the feet of (your) servants, and night and day have the sight of them;
offering body and mind, may I serve (your) servants, and with my tongue sing the Lord's praises.
With every breath may I remember my God, and let us ever remain in the company of the Sants.
The Naam is my one support and my wealth; O Nanak, this is the bliss to be gained. ॥2॥
533.4: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O friend, I have found such a dear Lord:
he never leaves and goes away, he is always with (me); meeting the Guru, I sing of him night and day.
I have met the Enchanter of the mind, the home of all peace; he does not forsake (me) to go anywhere.
I have seen many, of many and many kinds, (but none) equals a single hair of the Beloved.
In the temple (of the heart) there is good fortune, at the door there is glory, and the unstruck melody chimes softly.
Says Nanak, (one who has) settled for ever in the Beloved's home ever enjoys the joy of love. ॥2॥
533.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My mind longs for the sight (of the Lord) and for (his) Name.
It has wandered through every place, O brother, and, longing, has now fallen in behind the Sants.
Whom shall I serve, whom shall I worship? Whatever is seen passes away.
Let us seek the refuge of the Saadh Sangat; the mind craves the dust of (their) feet.
I know no way (across), and have no virtue at all; Maya is so very hard to cross.
Coming to the Guru, Nanak has fallen at his feet; then all evil desire was lifted. ॥2॥
534.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Your words, O Beloved, are Amrit;
O utterly beautiful, enchanting Beloved, (you are) within all, (yet) apart.
I do not want kingship, nor do I want liberation; (may) love for (your) lotus feet (dwell) in my mind.
Brahma, Shiva, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra (may be sought by others); for me, the sight of the Master alone.
Lowly, I have come to (your) door, O Master; worn out, I have fallen into the refuge of the Sants.
Says Nanak, God, the Enchanter of the mind, has met (me); my mind is cooled and in bloom. ॥2॥
534.2: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Lord's (Name), the servant has been carried across;
God, merciful to the meek, has become his own, and does not make him die again in (another) birth.
Let us sing the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat; (so) the jewel of human life is not lost.
Singing God's praises, (he) has crossed the poisonous waters of vice, and saved all his generations.
The lotus feet (of the Lord) dwell in his heart; with every breath and every morsel he has uttered (the Name).
Nanak has taken the shelter of the Lord of the world, and is a sacrifice (to him) again and again. ॥2॥
534.3: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(Some) wander in the forests wearing holy garbs, (yet) Mohan (the Enchanting Lord) stays apart (from them).
(Some) expound and recite, and sing lovely songs, (but) harbour filth in their minds.
(Some) are very handsome, very clever and wise, with learning and a graceful tongue.
Free of pride, attachment and (the sense of) mine and yours: this path is (walking) the edge of a double-edged sword (khanda).
Says Nanak, that one has crossed the world-ocean (who has), by God's grace, the company of the Sants. ॥4॥
534.4: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I have seen, O sister: Mohan is high, higher than all.
No other comes up to his level; I have searched a great deal, until weary.
He is utterly boundless, exceedingly great and deep; he has no bottom, and is high beyond grasp.
He cannot be weighed on any scale, nor bought at any price; where is the Delight of the mind to be found?
Countless have searched, many have practised austerities, (but) without the Guru none has reached (him).
Says Nanak, (when) the Master showed grace, meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I savoured (his) delight. ॥2॥
535.1: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have looked in many ways, O sister: there is no other at all.
He pervades all the regions and continents, and fills all the worlds.
He is beyond reach, utterly beyond reach; who (can tell) his greatness? Hearing of his glory, the mind comes alive.
(Those of) the four ashrams (stages of life) and the four varnas (castes) have been liberated, serving him.
The Guru has made the Shabad firm (within), and the supreme state is attained; duality is gone, and there is peace.
Says Nanak, the world-ocean has been crossed, and the Lord, the treasure, found in Sahaj. ॥2॥
535.2: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O brother, know the Lord as One, the One alone;
O brother, through the Guru know him as One.
Why do you wander? Do not wander, brother; he pervades, O brother, he pervades every place.
As fire is in the wood, (yet) without the right method it does not get the work done,
(so) without the Guru (none) will find the door of the dear Lord.
Joining the Sangat and casting off pride, says Nanak, (one) has found the supreme treasure. ॥2॥
535.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Where can I show (him) by any cleverness? Those who try to describe (him) are left wonderstruck upon wonderstruck.
The ganas (Shiva's attendants), the gandharvas (heavenly singers), the Siddhas and the seekers,
godlike men, the gods, Brahma and the gods like him,
and the four Vedas declare, by day and by night,
that the Master is beyond reach, beyond reach, and unfathomable.
Says Nanak, (his) virtues are endless, endless; (they) cannot be told; (he) is beyond the beyond. ॥2॥
535.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) meditates on the Creator and sings (his praises)
has no fear, (but) peace, Sahaj and bliss; O brother, he alone is the many: cherish (him), the One.
The Guru, whose presence bears fruit, (has his hand) upon my forehead;
wherever I look, there (he is) with me.
(His) lotus feet are the support of my life.
My God is all-powerful, fathomless and great;
the Master is near, within each and every heart.
Nanak has looked to the refuge and support of God, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥2॥
535.5: Raag Devgandhari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Turn back, O mind, turn back;
turn yourself away from the Saakat (one who has turned from God).
The love of the false one is false: it breaks off, O mind, it surely breaks off; in the Saakat's company there is no release.
As a house kept filled with lampblack blackens whoever goes into it, (so is the Saakat's company);
he has fled from it while still far off, the one whose trikuti (the frown of inner fretting) has left him on meeting the Guru.
O merciful one, treasure of mercy, I beg (this) gift of you: that my face may never be joined to a Saakat's.
Make servant Nanak the slave of (your) slaves; my head shall lie in the dust beneath the feet of the Saadhs. ॥2॥
536.1: Raag Devgandhari, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Bithal (God, who stands beyond Maya), I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, (to those) who at all times are able (to show) the path:
your Sants, who sing (your praise) and are dear to you; may I lie at their feet.
O you who are all compassion, (they are the ones) who have no craving, who delight in Sahaj, whose place is in the One, the infinite, the incomparable.
Riddhis (wealth and plenty), siddhis and the treasures are in the palms of your hands, O Life of the world, Master of all, (you of) countless Names.
Show kindness, tenderness and grace to Nanak, that I may live by hearing your praise again and again. ॥2॥
536.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
This mind does not do even a little of what it is told.
I have given it counsel as best I could, and am worn out; it does not turn from its evil understanding.
Gone mad with the intoxication of Maya, it does not utter the Lord's praise;
practising deceit, it cheats the world and fills its own belly.
Like a dog's tail, it never becomes straight; it pays no heed to what it is told.
Says Nanak, worship the Name of Ram always, by which (life's) purpose is fulfilled. ॥2॥
536.3: Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
All of it is a dealing only of the living:
mother, father, brothers, sons, kinsmen, and the wife of the house as well.
When the life-breath parts from the body, they cry out aloud and call (him) a pret (the dead).
No one keeps (him) even half a ghari; they put (him) out of the house.
The making of the world is like a mirage (the deer's thirst): reflect on this in your heart and see.
Says Nanak, worship the Name of Ram always, by which deliverance comes. ॥2॥
536.4: Raag Devgandhari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
In the world I have found love false.
All are attached only to their own comfort, be it wife or friend.
Everyone keeps saying, mine, mine; the mind is bound by attachment.
Yet at the last moment no one is a companion; this is a strange way (of the world).
O foolish mind, even now you do not understand, though I have grown weary of counselling you day after day.
O Nanak, when (a person) sings the songs of God, he crosses the terrifying world-ocean. ॥2॥
